## Summary

I implemented the audit-on-create requirement in the owner create endpoint (`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`, which handles `POST /api/owners`):

1. Added a dedicated SLF4J logger named `AUDIT`:
   ```java
   private static final Logger AUDIT = LoggerFactory.getLogger("AUDIT");
   ```

2. After the owner is successfully persisted (`saveOwner`), emit one audit line carrying the owner id, `customerCode`, and `registrationDate`:
   ```java
   this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
   AUDIT.info("owner created: id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
       owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
   ```

The line is emitted only on the success path (after all validation/quota/duplicate checks pass and the entity is saved), so failed creates produce no audit line. The `registrationDate` is logged via `LocalDate`'s ISO-8601 `toString()`, matching the value the DTO serializes and the test reads back from `GET /api/owners/{id}`. The new `AcceptanceTest.coreLogsAuditOnCreate` passes, and no existing tests regressed.
